questions.prompt: The model replies with a tool call that names get_weather and gives the city Paris. What has happened?
options: The model ran get_weather and read the weather itself
The model asked your program to run get_weather with Paris
The model wrote its final answer without any result
The model changed the tool schema to add a city field
questions.explanation: A tool call is a request, not an action. The model writes the name and the arguments, and your program decides whether to run the function.

questions.prompt: Why does a tool result carry the id of the call it answers?
options: So the result matches the call that asked for it
So the model can check that the result is true
So the result uses fewer tokens in the request
So the program can skip the tool schema
questions.explanation: The id on the result matches it to the call it answers, so the model knows which request the outcome belongs to.

questions.prompt: A tool schema has a name, a description and parameters. Which part tells the model which arguments the function accepts?
questions.explanation: The parameters part is a JSON Schema of the arguments. It gives the fields, their types and which fields are required, so the model can form a valid call.
